# Standards & federation

Dossiq declares the standards below in its manifest. OpenRegister publishes them to other servers without login, under `dossiq.discovery` in `/ocs/v2.php/cloud/capabilities`, so another instance can tell from a hostname alone whether it can connect. Tools such as [Nextcloud Peek](https://genhttp.dev/lambda/nextcloud-peek/) show it too.

## Standards this app uses

These are standards the app acts as a client of. They tell another server what this app can connect *to*.

| [Haal Centraal BRP Personen bevragen](https://brp-api.github.io/Haal-Centraal-BRP-bevragen/) | — |
| [BAG API Individuele Bevragingen](https://lvbag.github.io/BAG-API/) | 2 |
| Haal Centraal BRK Bevragen | 2 |
| [Haal Centraal WOZ Bevragen](https://kadaster.github.io/WOZ-bevragen/) | — |
| [KvK Handelsregister API](https://developers.kvk.nl/) | — |

## Federation (Open Cloud Mesh)

Dossiq registers no Open Cloud Mesh resource type of its own. Objects it stores in OpenRegister can still be shared with another instance through OpenRegister's `openregister` resource type.

## How another server finds this

```bash
curl -s -H 'OCS-APIRequest: true' \
  'https://cloud.example.org/ocs/v2.php/cloud/capabilities?format=json' \
  | jq '.ocs.data.capabilities["dossiq"].discovery'
```

Paths are relative to the instance root. Prefix `/index.php` when the instance runs without pretty URLs (`core.mod-rewrite-working` is false). Endpoints that need a Nextcloud login are listed without their path.

## Administrators

- Stop publishing discovery for every app: `occ config:app:set openregister discovery_public --value=no`
- Hide only this app: add `dossiq` to `occ config:app:set openregister discovery_hidden_apps --value=...` (comma separated)

Field reference and the shared list of standard ids: [Discovery and federation](https://github.com/ConductionNL/openregister/blob/development/docs/Technical/discovery-and-federation.md).
